goal: Vacation last-minute deals show today before 14:00 Israel time and tomorrow from 14:00 onward.

intent_model.literal_request: Show today and at 14:00 switch to tomorrow.
intent_model.implied_outcome: The displayed last-minute date, supplier request and automatic refresh all agree at the exact business cutoff.
likely_rejections: The switch happens one minute late.
The helper changes but the visible rail remains cached.
A weekend tab is moved by the last-minute rule.

interpretation_rules.operational_meaning: 14:00:00 Israel time is the first instant that uses tomorrow.

cognitive_flow.current_layer: The visitor sees the nearest bookable night appropriate to the current Israel time.
cognitive_flow.current_decision: Before 14:00 use today; from 14:00 use tomorrow.
cognitive_flow.next_action: The visitor opens a returned deal for the displayed dates.
deferred_complexity: Supplier booking confirmation remains in the existing booking flow.
preserved_depth: All four near-weekend tabs remain separately available.

facts.claim: The current last-minute period always adds one day.
The current shared clock changes at 14:01.

assumptions.claim: The cutoff uses Asia/Jerusalem for daylight-saving correctness.
assumptions.validation: Existing shared clock implementation and boundary tests use Asia/Jerusalem.

in_scope: Today before cutoff and tomorrow from cutoff
Automatic client refresh and cache identity
Regression coverage for weekend tabs and shared consumers
out_of_scope: Changes to supplier availability or pricing
invariants: Supplier data remains authoritative for availability and price.
The four weekend periods retain their weekday and night counts.
affected_family: Event and spa shared clock consumers

requirements.statement: Before 14:00 Israel time last-minute uses today.
At 14:00 Israel time last-minute switches to tomorrow.
The visible rail refreshes across the cutoff without stale cached dates.
Weekend periods and shared deal consumers do not regress.

acceptance_checks.observable_result: The request cache identity changes and a fresh date request is made.

acceptance_checks.setup: Dates immediately before and at the cutoff
acceptance_checks.action: Resolve every weekend period and run shared clock tests
acceptance_checks.observable_result: Weekend dates remain correct and shared consumers pass their date guards.

acceptance_checks.setup: A tab regains focus after crossing 14:00
acceptance_checks.action: Focus or visibility event refreshes the clock
acceptance_checks.observable_result: The current post-cutoff date is requested.

acceptance_checks.setup: A pre-cutoff response exists in the client discovery cache
acceptance_checks.observable_result: The post-cutoff request uses a different cache identity and cannot reuse the pre-cutoff date payload.

authorization_boundary: Local implementation and verification only. No production publication.
